$comment: Known parallel declarations. A name may be exported from more than one file only when the second site serves a bundle boundary that must not import the first. Adding an entry requires naming the canonical owner and the reason; removing one is always preferred. Verified by scripts/verify/check-declaration-ownership.ts.

resolveAcknowledgedProcessorLifecycle.reason: spectra.ui-control-runtime.ts is the slim Popup entry and restates the lifecycle projection so the popup bundle does not pull the control contracts table.

isMediaTarget.reason: spectra.content-runtime.ts is the slim Content entry; it keeps only the guards the content host can actually exercise.

isSpectraRequestEnvelope.reason: Two protocol entries by design: Content aliases the slim entry in production, every other context keeps the complete validator. This pair must stay behaviourally identical; unknown payload types are rejected on both sides.

isSpectraResponse.reason: Same bundle split as isSpectraRequestEnvelope. The two differ on unlisted response types by construction - the slim entry only knows what Content can receive - so a change to either must be mirrored deliberately.

sameMediaTarget.reason: Background tolerates null targets; Content requires a resolved target and lives in a different bundle. Merging them would give one side semantics it never needs.

getActionName.reason: Options resolves from a bundled static dictionary; Content resolves from the loaded locale catalog. Same verb, different data source per host.

sendSpectraRequest.reason: Two host adapters exposing the same verb surface: one sends from Content, one from Popup/Options. They cannot share because the transport lease and sender context differ.
